Hi Alice - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the items we said we would confirm about prompt/output handling and retention: 

1) What Redwood stores by default for Hosted API: request/response logs (full prompt + model output) are retained for 30 days by default to support debugging, billing, and abuse prevention. Logs are stored encrypted at rest in the account region (we discussed EU region).

2) Training use: Redwood does not use customer prompts/outputs to train public models. Customer data is not incorporated into our model training without an explicit contractual agreement.

3) Embeddings and storage: embeddings are only persisted if you opt into embeddings storage (e.g., for semantic search). If you do store embeddings, raw text is not stored by default unless you configure a document store; we can provide redaction guidance.

4) Options for stricter controls: Dedicated/Private deployments can be configured to keep logs entirely within your VPC/on-prem and retention can be reduced to 0 days per contract. For Hosted accounts we offer an enterprise option to disable/request zero retention and to limit what metadata is kept.

5) Audit & compliance: SOC 2 Type II in-place, logs and audit trails available to admins per role-based controls. We can share a redacted SOC2 report and a DPA.

Next steps I proposed on the call: 
- I'll introduce Neha (cc'ed) from Security to answer the technical retention/residency questions and confirm specific controls around masking/redaction.
- If Acme prefers 0-day retention for prompts/outputs on Hosted, we can scope that in the contract and technical implementation options for the EU region.

Can you confirm: (a) you want default Hosted logging reduced to zero for prompts/outputs, (b) you need embeddings disabled/purged, and (c) any specific retention requirement for audit logs (e.g., 90 days read-only)? Once we have that we can give a concrete contract language and timeline.

Thanks - happy to hop on a short call with Neha if helpful.

Hi Alice / Rishi - thanks, and happy to provide a concise confirmation for your security team. Summary below - I'll also attach the redacted SOC 2 and our DPA.

Key items (short answers):
- Where data is stored: For Hosted accounts we store logs in the cloud region tied to your account (EU region: AWS eu-west-1). Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256; customer-managed KMS keys are available for Enterprise accounts.

- What is stored by default: 
  * Full request/response logs (prompt + output) - default retention 30 days for Hosted.
  * Request metadata (request_id, timestamp, route, model version, token counts) - retained for 30 days by default.
  * Admin/audit events (user actions in Console) - retained for 90 days and can be exported to your SIEM.

- Zero-retention option for prompts/outputs: 
  * Hosted: we offer an enterprise configuration to not persist request/response bodies (prompts/outputs). In that mode we retain only minimal metadata (request_id, timestamp, model identifier) for operational troubleshooting. No raw prompt/output bodies are written to persistent logs. This is configurable and will be included in contract language and scoped engineering work for the EU region.
  * Dedicated/Private: logs remain inside your VPC/on-prem and retention is fully customer-controlled; we can set retention to 0 in those deployments.

- Embeddings: 
  * Embeddings are only persisted if you enable embeddings storage (e.g., for search). When persisted, we store the vector and an optional document id; storing raw source text is optional and off by default. We support purge APIs to delete embeddings on demand and can provide export logs for deletion events.

- Using data for training: Redwood does not use customer prompts/outputs to train models or improve public models without explicit opt-in in contract.

- Audit logs / 90-day requirement: 
  * We can provide a 90-day immutable admin audit trail for console/admin actions and role changes without retaining prompt/output bodies. Those admin logs are separated from request bodies and can be exported to your SIEM (S3, Splunk, or LogRhythm) on demand.

- Access controls & encryption: Role-based access controls limit who at Redwood can access logs; all access is logged and requires justification for support tickets. Enterprise customers get additional access controls and optional customer-managed keys.
